items.title: [dagenslantbruk.se] Swedish farmers’ federation says spring budget leaves input-cost crisis unresolved
items.content_html: The Federation of Swedish Farmers (LRF) said Sweden’s spring budget failed to ease high farm costs, especially for diesel and fertilizer, even as policymakers call for increased domestic food production. Farmer representatives on Arla’s board said cheaper groceries do not necessarily mean lower production costs. LRF president Palle Borgström said higher costs could force some farm businesses to stop production and urged the government to prevent EU climate tariffs from making fertilizer more expensive. The budget increased funding for food and water preparedness and nitrogen-efficiency investments, but LRF said it did not address farmers’ most urgent economic pressures.

items.title: [scotsman.com] European researchers test farm water systems as climate swings threaten crops
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Scotland’s summer of 2026 brought earlier harvests, heat stress in spring-sown crops and rapidly falling water levels, while research indicates extreme day-to-night temperature swings have become more frequent since the 1980s. Those swings can disrupt crop growth. The Scotsman reported Scottish cereal yields below historic averages, with results varying by crop, soil and location. A Swedish research project is testing a retention-irrigation system that stores water during dry periods and releases it during floods to develop recommendations for its use. In Spain, agricultural cooperatives say farmers are working to adapt and cut emissions but warn that putting innovations into practice depends on farm profitability and adequate funding under the next EU farm-policy reform.

items.title: [therecord.media] Microsoft links ConnectWise breach to China-aligned AI hacking group
items.content_html:
🎨 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

Microsoft on Oct. 21 attributed the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain breach to Storm-0940, a China-aligned hacking group that used the ARTEX AI framework in a campaign targeting hundreds of organizations worldwide. The attackers used compromised ConnectWise application identities and permissions already granted to those apps to access customers' Microsoft 365 environments without an interactive user sign-in. Microsoft said Storm-0940 attempted to access more than 2,250 tenants and, in several cases, gained privileged cloud access less than three hours after selecting a target. ARTEX automated scanning, reconnaissance, password spraying and abuse of application permissions. Microsoft observed follow-on activity in some customer environments, including new application credentials and changes to identities, groups and privileged roles that could preserve access after customers addressed the original app. Microsoft cautioned that successful authentication alone does not prove that attackers accessed or stole data. ConnectWise said Oct. 22 that it was restoring services in phases over several days and told customers to keep affected connections disabled until they receive service-specific instructions. The company said its existing backup archives remained encrypted, isolated and preserved, with no indication they were compromised.
